identity.title: The Regulation of Hypoxia Inducible Factor (HIF)1alpha Expression by Quercetin: an In Silico Study.

content.abstract: BACKGROUND: Cancer disease is a growing health problem in developing and developed countries. Hypoxia-inducible factor-1a (HIF1alpha) is a transcription factor responsible for expressing several proteins involved in angiogenesis. Quercetin can suppress HIF1alpha expression due to the inhibition of protein synthesis. However, to date, the study exploring the potential of quercetin in repressing HIF1alpha through its degradation mechanism has never been done. An in silico study is needed as a preliminary study to understand the mechanism underlining this possibility. OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to investigate the potential of quercetin in regulating HIF1alpha expression through the ubiquitin degradation pathway by in silico study. METHODS: This study was performed by in silico analysis, including biological activity prediction, 3D protein structure collection, protein-ligand and protein-protein docking, and the visualization of the docking results. RESULTS: The probability activity (Pa) score of quercetin as an HIF1alpha expression inhibitor was 0.969. In the absence of quercetin, the center-weighted score of HIF1alpha - pVHL, HIF1alpha - FIH, and HIF1alpha - PHD2 was -699.4 kJ/mol, -846.0 kJ/mol, and -650.5 kJ/mol, respectively. In the presence of quercetin, the weighted score of HIF1alpha - pVHL, HIF1alpha - FIH, and HIF1alpha - PHD2 was reduced to -728.1 kJ/mol, -854.2 kJ/mol, and -650.5 kJ/mol, respectively. CONCLUSION: Quercetin could directly promote HIF1alpha and pVHL interaction, thus increasing the degradation of HIF1alpha by ubiquitin-dependent pathway.
